A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KL-Shampoo research, with v3 expanding its scope to SOAP and alternative estimation schemes. Text, equations, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including v1 Appendices A–C and v3 Appendices A–H.

before.justification: v1 Section 5 and Figures 1–2 report original language-model training experiments, including test-loss curves against training steps and elapsed time.

after.justification: v3 Section 6 and Appendix H report original training comparisons and component analyses, including results for KL-SOAP, F-Shampoo, and VN-Shampoo.

M1.justification: Alongside the retained KL-Shampoo approach, v3 introduces KL-SOAP, which applies Adam/RMSProp in KL-Shampoo’s estimated eigenbasis (Section 5). It also adapts the QR and eigenvalue-averaging procedures to Frobenius-based and trace-scaled Shampoo variants, with explicit update schemes in Figures 6 and 8.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate NanoGPT and NanoRWKV7 on FineWeb, Llama on C4, and NanoMoE on OpenWebText, with the same stated model sizes and token subsets. The additional analyses use NanoGPT and Llama from this retained coverage; they introduce no new dataset, task, or domain.

E2.justification: v1 compares KL-Shampoo with Shampoo using powers 1/2 and 1/4, with and without grafting, and SOAP. v3 adds KL-SOAP to the runtime comparison and evaluates two-sided Frobenius-based F-Shampoo and trace-scaled VN-Shampoo variants (Figures 5, 7, 9, and 10). Figure 5 also evaluates an adapted Shampoo comparator using QR and eigenvalue averaging.

E3.justification: The stated hyperparameter-search budget increases from 120 to 150 trials per method; v3 specifies two stages of 75 trials, first broad and then refined. Separately, new experiments introduce controlled comparisons of instantaneous versus averaged eigenvalues and align implementations and QR/EMA procedures across estimation schemes. The retained model sizes, token subsets, batch sizes, and default decomposition interval remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds an explicit eigenvalue-averaging ablation under outdated eigenbases (Figure 4), controlled comparisons of one-sided and two-sided estimation and divergence choices (Figure 5), and analyses of QR/EMA adaptations for F-Shampoo and VN-Shampoo (Appendix H). These investigate component contributions beyond the grafting comparisons already present in v1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The change from 120 to 150 runs concerns hyperparameter-search trials and does not establish a change in repeated-run statistical reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds KL-SOAP training curves, reports KL-Shampoo outperforming KL-SOAP, and supplies new findings about eigenvalue averaging and the relative performance of F-Shampoo and VN-Shampoo. The reported unsuccessful ungrafted Shampoo 1/2 searches on RWKV7 increase from 120 to 150. The revised main curves accompany a changed search budget, so they do not establish performance gains under an unchanged evaluation protocol.

T1.justification: v1’s eigenvalue Claim 3 and proof become v3 Claim 4 and Appendix D. v3 adds Claims 3, 5, 6, and 7 with derivations covering proximal-gradient averaging, augmented SOAP eigenvalues, Frobenius estimation, and VN/Adafactor relationships. Claims 2 and 4 are qualified as conditions satisfied at an optimum. The new Appendix C formal update nevertheless omits dimension-normalization factors present in Equation 5 and its own subsequent derivation.

C1.justification: The central contribution expands from interpreting and improving Shampoo to a unified treatment of Shampoo and SOAP, including the new KL-SOAP method. The abstract and introduction additionally claim KL-Shampoo outperforms KL-SOAP and that the practical techniques can make trace-scaled Shampoo competitive without grafting.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of eigenvalue averaging as correction for outdated eigenbases in Kronecker-factored versus augmented diagonal spaces, a matrix-Gaussian whitening interpretation, and discussion of KL versus VN applicability. It also explicitly qualifies exact optimality when expectations are approximated and identifies limited computation as the reason appendix experiments cover only two models.

D1.justification: Table 1 and its associated footnote newly disclose bfloat16 storage and updates, with QR/eigendecomposition performed in float32 before casting. Section 6 further identifies tuned parameters and implementation sources. These improve documentation; v1 does not establish that a different precision regime was previously used.

R1.justification: v3 substantially broadens positioning through connections to KL-based BFGS/DFP interpretations, matrix-normal maximum-likelihood estimation, Bregman matrix divergences, and Adafactor. Added references such as Fletcher, Dutilleul, Kanamori and Ohara, and Shazeer and Stern support these substantive relationships.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are substantially rewritten around the joint Shampoo/SOAP framework. Background and method explanations expand considerably, while the short preliminary-results narrative becomes a discussion organized around four experimental questions and additional appendix analyses.

P2.justification: The original runtime and step-wise plots become v3 Figures 1 and 2, with revised colors, legends, and axis presentation. Figure 3 gains a SOAP/KL-SOAP panel. v3 also adds the memory table, algorithm diagrams in Figures 6 and 8, and analysis plots in Figures 4, 5, 7, 9, and 10.

improvement.justification: v1 mainly supports its design through aggregate preliminary training comparisons. v3 Figures 4–5 and Appendix H add component analyses and matched comparisons that substantially strengthen evidence for eigenvalue averaging and the choice of estimation rule. Memory and precision disclosures also improve assessability. Appendix C introduces a normalization inconsistency between its formal claim and derivation, but this localized defect does not outweigh the substantial improvement in empirical support.
